claims.text: The starting alloy is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The starting HfNbTaTiZr alloy is in the cast state.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxidation resistance for high-temperature use in air.
A 5–10 nm ALD-deposited Al2O3 coating is an appropriate anti-oxidation intervention for cast HfNbTaTiZr.
ALD will produce a conformal, dense, continuous Al2O3 layer on the alloy.
The ultrathin Al2O3 layer will prevent or substantially impede oxygen ingress into the bulk alloy.
Suppressing oxygen diffusion through the coating will mitigate oxidation of the underlying alloy.
The surface coating will not alter the intrinsic cast microstructure.
The intrinsic cast microstructure is responsible for the alloy's useful mechanical properties.
After 100 hours at 1000 °C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere, coated specimens will have significantly lower weight gain or thinner oxide scales than uncoated specimens.
The coated alloy will retain room-temperature tensile ductility within 8–16% after oxidation exposure.
The coated alloy will retain high-temperature yield strength within 163–530 MPa after oxidation exposure.
The claimed protection applies at strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^-2 s^-1.
Coating integrity must be maintained during high-temperature exposure and tensile loading for the intervention to work.
Long-term stability of the ultrathin ALD alumina coating under cyclic thermal stress has not been established.
Interfacial delamination may limit the coating's performance.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that specimens undergo tensile loading during the 100-hour oxidation exposure, whereas the experimental design exposes specimens first and conducts tensile tests afterward.
